label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.10 a.2…: What is altogether IMMUTABLE_1, in potency in no…
locator: I q.10 a.2 co.: ratio aeternitatis consequitur immutabilitatem, sicut ratio temporis consequitur motum
interpretation: The notion of eternity follows immutability as the notion of time follows motion; with a.1 (what is altogether immutable has neither succession nor beginning nor end, the two marks of eternity). Read as: what is in potency in no respect (altogether immutable, with no capacity for any change) is eternal. Not 'not changing now', which the prima via's present-tense MovedIn would give and which would make any momentarily unchanging creature eternal (Codex P1 on #199). Eternal is a primitive predicate whose content a.1 gives; only this sufficient condition is formalized.
